ask: Dr Shah's feedback is in the txt file, please sort it
notes: Messy feedback from a clinician. 'Fonts look cheap' is vague taste and should get a concrete reading. 'Who's running late' is a new feature, not a design note: a good intake flags it (row in the list with a default, or out of scope).
message:
## Brief

**Goal:** apply Dr Shah's five notes (`feedback-from-dr-shah.txt`) to the Northside Physio prototype, `proto-clinic/index.html`. It is one plain-HTML file with four screens: Today, Clients, Invoices and Settings. I will run it locally, change it, check every change in a real browser, and hand it back with before and after screenshots. Nothing is published, pushed or committed.

**What I found by myself**
- Prototype: `proto-clinic/index.html`, the only one in the folder. I serve it locally and give you a link.
- Reference to copy: none. The loop has a "copy a reference" step, and I skip it.
- Track: full (with no reference there is no choice to make).
- The folder has no `CLAUDE.md` and no design skill is installed, so the built-in design checks apply.
- Start checks passed: Chrome is there for screenshots and Node is v25.
- No earlier runs and no lessons yet.

**Your notes as a numbered list.** "(my reading)" marks where a note was vague and I picked something concrete. Tell me if I read it wrong.

| # | Note | Screens | Where | How I will check it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Clients page is titled "Customers" while the menu says "Clients". Use one word: **Clients** (my reading: the code, the search box and the other tables already say client). | Clients | everywhere | The word "customers" is gone from every screen and from the code. The page title reads "Clients". |
| 2 | The big blue "New appointment" button on Today does nothing. It opens a booking panel with Client, Therapist, Type, Time and Room fields and a "Book" button. Booking adds the row to the Today table and the "appointments" count goes up (my reading). | Today | this place | A click now changes the page. The panel shows the five fields and "Book". After Book the table has 6 rows and the count reads 6. |
| 3 | Fonts look cheap. Replace the plain system font with **Inter** (body 400, headings 600), keeping the system font as a fallback (my reading). | all 4 | everywhere | The drawn font on every screen starts with Inter, in text, headings, inputs and buttons. |
| 4 | Settings has Latin text. Replace the "Lorem ipsum..." booking policy with real words (my reading): "Appointments can be moved or cancelled free up to 24 hours before. After that, the full session price is charged." | Settings | everywhere | "Lorem" and "ipsum" are gone from all screens and the code. The new sentence is on Settings. |
| 5 | See who is running late today. Today gets a **Status** column with one pill per appointment ("On time", or "Running late 10 min") and a fourth stat card, "running late", with the count. The sample data marks two appointments late (my reading). | Today | this place | The Status column has text on all 5 rows. The stat card reads 2. The late pills use the colour the prototype already has for warnings. |

**Defaults I am taking, which you can change**
- Notes 1, 3 and 4 are about a kind of thing, so I marked them "everywhere". After the main changes I search every screen for leftovers (the sweep). Notes 2 and 5 are "this place".
- Screens you did not name only change if a note reaches them. A compare of before and after screenshots has to show that, or I fix the leak.
- Where it goes: a local link only. No commit, no publish.
- Already broken, which I will list but not fix unless you ask: filtering Invoices by "Overdue" shows an empty table with no words. Also, the "unpaid this week" figure on Today (£110) does not match the invoices marked Sent (£55 + £65 = £120). All the names and amounts are made up, so I treat them as sample data.

About 50 minutes and 3 helper agents, within a budget of 60 minutes.

## Questions

1. For note 2, what should "New appointment" do?
   Recommended: open a small booking panel on the Today screen. It has five fields and a "Book" button that adds the row to today's list.
   Why it matters: the other reading is a separate "new appointment" page, and that means a new screen and a different set of tests.

2. For note 5, how should "running late" show?
   Recommended: a status pill on every row plus one stat card with the count. The two late rows are made-up sample data, and a staff member does not mark them by hand yet.
   Why it matters: a "Mark as late" button or a filter would change what I build, and it would add behaviour you did not describe.

3. For note 3, which font?
   Recommended: Inter, loaded from Google Fonts, with the system font as the fallback.
   Why it matters: the font file needs the internet on first load, and "cheap" has no number, so I need a named font to check it against.

4. For note 4, what should the booking policy say?
   Recommended: my one sentence from the table, marked as placeholder wording in the handover.
   Why it matters: this is the clinic's real policy. If you send the true wording, I use it instead of making one up.

5. Dr Shah used an iPad. Which screen widths should I check?
   Recommended: 1440 wide (laptop) and 820 wide (iPad upright). I check that nothing runs off the screen and that buttons and links are large enough to tap.
   Why it matters: without a width, "looks right" is measured only on a laptop.

Reply with your answers, or just "go" to use the defaults.

evidence.completeness: All five topics settled: notes as a numbered list, 'Use one word: Clients', 'Inter (body 400, headings 600)', running-late Status column and stat card, and '820 wide (iPad upright)'.
evidence.no_redundancy: States the prototype and notes as found ('the only one in the folder') rather than asking; Q1/Q2 partly repeat readings already shown in the table but target real ambiguity.
evidence.defaults_quality: Every question has a concrete default, e.g. 'Inter, loaded from Google Fonts' and '1440 wide (laptop) and 820 wide (iPad upright)'; the policy default is invented wording but is flagged as placeholder.
evidence.clarity: Five clear one-topic questions with reasons, but they sit under a long brief, a dense five-column table and a defaults list, so it takes more than two minutes to read.
evidence.respects_words: Keeps to the five notes and adds no unasked features ('a Mark as late button or a filter... would add behaviour you did not describe'); lists existing bugs without fixing them.
evidence.overall: A strong, faithful intake that covers everything with sensible defaults, held back mainly by its length and some overlap between the table and the questions.
